claim: Markdown in Git is the authoritative memory while SQLite is explicitly derived and rebuildable, preserving inspectability and portability without giving up structured retrieval.
Cross-agent continuation is modeled as a typed, claim-once handoff protocol rather than a prompt convention, with cwd/project scoping and lifecycle semantics.

claim: Retrieval fuses FTS, entity, graph-neighbor and optional vector streams with RRF, then applies bounded authority rather than letting metadata become an absolute override.
The self-improvement loop is separated from hook latency, stages validated proposals, supports approval/eval gates, and now includes retry/parking semantics for failed scheduled reviews.
Capture has an explicit typed privacy boundary: bounded bodies, client/server sanitization paths, opt-in assistant capture, host/network hardening, and stored-content prompt-injection treatment.

claim: Engineering discipline is unusually high for a young repo: workspace-wide tests, nextest profiles, secret scanning, unsafe Rust forbidden, and broad integration-test coverage across crates.
The security model is intentionally single-trust-domain: no tenant isolation, no per-user private memory ACLs, and no encryption at rest in v1.
Markdown-primary plus SQLite-derived indexing has no true cross-resource transaction; crash windows rely on rollback best-effort and later reindex reconciliation.
Several core source files are very large (for example MCP server/admin and store reader/ops), raising navigation, review, ownership, and change-coupling costs despite crate-level modularity.

Provider-backed auto-improvement can auto-approve validated proposals by default; strong gates exist, but operators must understand the trust boundary because learned changes can become durable memory.

Historical recall is not merely timestamps on current pages: the as_of path resolves page/entity validity windows and version-filtered lexical search while deliberately excluding present-tense vector/graph streams.

Managed workstreams add portable continuity across harness-native sessions using an append-only normalized ledger and controlled session adoption rather than scraping all private agent stores indiscriminately.
